1theorem proposition_4 : ∀ (a b c : Point) (AB : Line),

3 |(a─b)| * |(a─b)| =
4 |(a─c)| * |(a─c)| + |(c─b)| * |(c─b)| + 2 * (|(a─c)| * |(c─b)|) :=

7 euclid_intro_sentence "2.4.0"►
8 "If a straight-line is cut at random, (then) the square on the whole (straight-line) is equal to the (sum of the) squares on the pieces (of the straight-line), and twice the rectangle contained by the pieces. For let the straight-line $AB$ be cut, at random, at (point) $C$. I say that the square on $AB$ is equal to the (sum of the) squares on $AC$ and $CB$, and twice the rectangle contained by $AC$ and $CB$."
